chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil-Khattab and Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazal, on the authority of Ali ibn Asbat, on the authority of al-Hussein ibn Zayd, who said: Muhammad ibn Salim narrated to me, linking it up to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).

He said: Uthman ibn Affan asked, 'O Messenger of God, what is the interpretation of Abjad?' The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Learn the interpretation of Abjad, for it contains all the wonders. Woe to a scholar who does not know its interpretation.' He asked, 'O Messenger of God, what is the interpretation of Abjad?'

He said: As for the Alif, it is the blessings (Ala') of God, a letter from His Names. And as for the Ba, it is the joy (Bahja) of God. And as for the Jim, it is the Paradise (Jannah) of God, His Beauty (Jamal), and His Majesty (Jalal). And as for the Dal, it is the Religion (Din) of God. And as for Huwaz, the Ha is the letter of the Abyss (Al-Hawiya): Woe to him who is cast into the Fire. And as for the Waw, it is Woe (Wayl) to the People of the Fire. And as for the Zay, it is a corner (Zawiya) in Hell; we seek refuge in God from what is in the corner, meaning the corners of Hell.

And as for Hata, the Ha is the shedding down (Hutut) of sins from those seeking forgiveness on the Night of Power, and what descended with it Gabriel (peace be upon him) with the angels until the emergence of dawn. And as for the Ta, it is Tooba for them and a good return; it is a tree that God, the Exalted, planted with His Hand and blew into it from His Spirit, and its branches are seen from behind the wall of Paradise, growing with jewelry, garments, and fruits, hanging over their mouths.

And as for the Ya, it is the Hand of God above His creation, Glorified and Exalted is He from what they associate. And as for Kalman, the Kaf is the Speech (Kalam) of God: 'No change in the words of God,' and 'You will not find besides Him a refuge.' And as for the Lam, it is the association of the People of Paradise with one another in visitation, greeting, and peace, and the mutual blaming of the People of Hell with one another.

And as for the Mim, it is the Dominion (Mulk) of God that does not fade, and the Permanence of God that does not perish. And as for the Nun, 'Nun. And the Pen and what they write.' The Pen is a pen of light, and the Book is a book of light, in a Preserved Tablet, witnessed by the Near Ones, and sufficient is God as Witness. As for Sa'fas, the Sad is 'a measure for a measure,' meaning recompense for recompense, as you judge, you are judged; indeed, God does not intend injustice for the servants.

And as for Qarshat, it means their gathering (Hashr) and their dispersal (Nashr) to the Day of Judgment, so judgment was passed between them with truth and they are not wronged. And I have included what I narrated regarding this meaning in the interpretation of the letters of the alphabet in my book Ma'ani al-Akhbar.

key_terms.أَبْجَد: Abjad (the first four letters of the Arabic alphabet, used here as a mnemonic for the whole alphabet)
key_terms.صَاعٌ بِصَاعٍ: A measure for a measure (recompense for recompense)
key_terms.طُوبَى: Tooba (a tree in Paradise or a cry of bliss)

ai.seo_question: What is the esoteric interpretation of the Arabic alphabet letters in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith presents an esoteric exegesis of the 'Abjad' letters, attributing each to divine attributes, eschatological realities, and Quranic concepts. It highlights the Shia emphasis on the mystical dimensions of language, where the alphabet serves as a key to understanding God’s names and the structure of the afterlife, warning against ignorance of this hidden knowledge.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-30 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil-Khat’tab and Ahmad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faz’zal, on the authority of Ali ibn Asbat, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Zayd, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Salim who linked it up through a chain of narrators to the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB), “Uthman ibn Affan asked the Prophet (MGB), ‘O Prophet of God!

What is the interpretation of ‘Abjad?’ The Prophet (MGB) said, ‘You should know the interpretation of ‘Abjad since all the wonders lie in it. Shame on a scholar who doesn’t know its interpretation!’ He asked, ‘O Prophet of God! What is the interpretation of ‘Abjad?’

The Prophet (MGB) said, ‘And the ‘alif is the first letter in Allah. It is one of the letters of His Name. And the ‘ba is the first letter in the Arabic ‘Behjat Allah which means God’s Pleasure. And the ‘jim is the first letter of the Arabic words ‘jinnah Allah which mean God’s Paradise; ‘jamal Allah which means God’s Beauty and ‘jalal Allah which means God’s Majesty. And the ‘dal is the first letter in the Arabic words ‘Din Allah which mean God’s Religion.About ‘hawaz’, you should know that the ‘ha is for fear of Hell. Shame on him who is thrown into the Fire of Hell. And the ‘wa is the second letter in the Arabic words ‘fawayl le ahlen Nar which means shame on in ‘Shame on the residents of the Fire.’ And the ‘za is the first letter in the Arabic word ‘zaviaa which refers to a corner - God forbid - from the various corners of Hell.

The ‘hata is the first letter in the Arabic word ‘hutut which refers to the shedding down of the sins of those who repent on the Night of Power on which Gabriel and all the angels pray all night until dawn. And about the ‘T in ‘Fatooba lahum va hosne ma’ab (Usually translated as ‘Blessed be’) you should know that Tooba is a tree which the Honorable the Exalted God planted with his own Hand, and blew into it from His own Spirit! Tooba is the name of a Heavenly tree which is rooted in the Prophet’s (MGB) house. Its branches can be seen from the outside the walls around Paradise.

And about the ‘Ya it refers to ‘Yadullah - that is God’s Hand which is above all His creatures. He is Glorified, and Sublime and has no partners. And the ‘kaf in ‘kalman refers to ‘Kalamullah implying that there can be no changing of God’s sayings and there are no protectors other than God. And the ‘lam in ‘kalman refers to the associations of the residents of Paradise; their visiting one another; and their greeting each other. It also refers to the mutual blaming of the residents of Hell.

And the ‘mim in ‘kalman refers to God’s Dominion which never ends and God’s Persistence which never ends. The ‘nun in ‘kalman refers to ‘Nun. By the Pen and the (Record) which (men) write.’ And the Pen is from Light; the Record is from Light. They are on a Tablet that is safeguarded. The nearby-stationed angels are witnesses to it. Their testimony suffices for God. The ‘sad in ‘safas refers to ‘sa which means a scale by which everything you do is measured. Indeed God would not stand any oppressions be done to the people.

The ‘qarasht means that God will resurrect them and bring them all back on the Resurrection Day and judge them.”Sadooq added, “I have compiled whatever is related to the meaning of the letters of the alphabet in ‘Abjad in my book Ma’ani al-Akhbar.”
